sub_indicators.label: National standards for information technology and data
sub_indicators.subject: gov.standards
sub_indicators.text: National quality standards: national standards for information technology and data
sub_indicators.norm_short: The Abuja Treaty, Article 67, commits member states to a common policy on standardisation and quality assurance, and the Pan-African Quality Infrastructure is the continent's platform. Neither says what standards for information technology or data should be.
criteria: A source from the past three years says the country has no national standards body.
A national standards body exists: a body set up by a law or decree to write or adopt national standards. One announced and not yet created does not count.

The body has issued a national standard on information technology or data: a named standard on information technology, information security, software or data, issued or adopted as a national standard. A national quality policy, telecoms quality-of-service rules and quality management standards do not count.

An organisation can be certified against such a standard in the country: the standards body, or a certifier accredited in the country, offers certification against it or has certified an organisation. A certificate from a certifier abroad does not count.

A public body has been certified in the past three years: a dated source names a ministry, agency or state-owned body certified against such a standard by the standards body or a certifier accredited in the country. How good the standards are is not judged.
